newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Banks boot Australian stocks higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Banks boot Australian stocks higher at open.

text.p: The Australian share market opened higher on Wednesday, led by a banking sector that outperformed the broader market after a better than expected first half result from Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
The bank reported an 11 percent rise in net profit to A$602 million (US$458 million) for the half year to December 31.
The All Ordinaries index added 9.20 points to 2,457.3.
"It looks like a good result," said dealer Nick Atkinson of brokerage Wilson HTM. However, he said a weaker resources sector, particularly in the golds, was weighing on the market.
"Golds are a little softer and that is weighing on it a bit," he said.

Commonwealth Bank resumed its role as star of the show with its shares heading back towards the top of its recent record range. The stock reached a record A$13.79 before easing back to A$13.70 in late morning trade, up 29 cents from Tuesday's close.
Gawler Craton gold hopeful Helix Resources slid again and was down over 11 percent at A$3.31 after Monday's drilling results failed to meet high expectations.

Business services group Ausdoc fell 10 percent to A$2.00 following Tuesday's late announcement by would-be suitor Brambles Industries that it would not increase its A$2.00 per share bid for the company.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to four, while about 40 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
